picks.file: Mosul, Illustration for La Terre-Sainte et les lieux illustrés par les apôtres, by Adrien Egron, 1837 (30).jpg
picks.what: The city across the Tigris from the Nineveh side, engraving in Adrien Egron, La Terre-Sainte
picks.why: general view of the walled city and its riverside castle across the water, labeled Mosul in the book

picks.file: Iraq. Mosul. General view with tall minaret in center of picture LOC matpc.16200.jpg
picks.what: The old city with the leaning al-Hadba minaret, photograph (Library of Congress, Matson Collection)
picks.why: rooftop view across the old city to its best-known landmark, destroyed in 2017; negative border trimmed off

gaps: P0–P2: nothing usable (siege miniatures and a battle print with an imaginary city, a map, and a view of Hilla mislabeled as Mosul); P6: nothing (photos of Maqlub Mountain and of mosque doors in Istanbul)
notes: The 1876 Newman engraving across the Tigris (#8) is attractive but only 15 years after the existing 1861 view, so it was not added. The 1837 engraving is somewhat idealized (the Tigris looks like a lake) but follows the usual view from the Nineveh mounds.
